status: designed, not yet executed -- Foundry Phases 4-6 (live execution, grading, benchmarking) not run

evals.prompt: I have a MySQL database and a SQL Server database, both need their schemas documented and diagrammed against our data dictionary. What's the plan?
expectations: Recommends sqlalchemy.inspect() as one shared code path for both engines rather than proposing separate custom scripts per engine.
Recommends pyodbc for the SQL Server connection, not pymssql, citing its uncertain maintenance status.
States that diagram generation is a separate step from schema interrogation, not bundled into the same tool.
Names the three severity tiers (P1/P2/P3) as the classification scheme for any deviations found against the data dictionary.

evals.prompt: Can you pull the schema out of this old Access database and tell me what's actually in it?
expectations: States plainly that the Access path (pyodbc+ODBC driver or COM/DAO) is less reliable than the SQLAlchemy path for other engines, not presented with equal confidence.
Names at least one concrete Access-specific limitation (Windows-only ODBC driver reliance, or mdbtools' known reliability issues on Linux/Mac).
Notes that DAO/COM can often read linked-table metadata without being able to open the records behind an external link.
Does not silently fall back to attempting Firestore/NoSQL-style document sampling or any out-of-scope technique.

evals.prompt: Just give me an ER diagram of these three tables, I already know the schema, here's the JSON.
expectations: Uses the schema-inventory JSON shape directly (entities/columns/relationships keys) without re-deriving it from a live database connection.
References the to_mermaid_erdiagram function or scripts/schema_to_mermaid.py by name as the mechanism used.
Produces valid Mermaid erDiagram syntax with entity attribute lines in the type/name/constraint/note format.
Does not introduce eralchemy2, Graphviz, or any other third-party ER-diagram library into the response.

evals.prompt: Here's my schema inventory JSON -- the relationships only have from/to/label plus fk_nullable and fk_unique, I didn't specify cardinality. Generate the ER diagram.
expectations: References infer_cardinality() by name as the mechanism that derives cardinality from fk_nullable/fk_unique, rather than asking the user to supply cardinality manually.
States that a NOT-NULL, non-unique FK infers to a required one-to-many operator (||--|{), distinguishing it from a nullable FK's optional one-to-many (||--o{).
States that a unique FK infers to a one-to-one operator (||--|| or ||--|o depending on nullability), not a one-to-many operator.
Notes that fk_nullable and fk_unique are already available from sqlalchemy.inspect()'s get_columns()/get_unique_constraints() output, not from an extra query.
